messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: streaming-tail-p99 > 2s across prod (alert: https://grafana.company/reports/alerts/streaming-p99)
Maria: I'm on it. Observed user-facing streaming stalls, p99 jumped ~2.1s at 16:02 UTC. Any recent infra rollouts? @Kevin were there kernel/tooling changes this morning?
Kevin: yes — TRT8/flashattn runtime + a new compilepath flag (-faggressive-kv) rolled at ~14:10 UTC. Build id: toolchain-2026-03-15-1420. Canary looked fine but canary traffic was low.
Susan: metrics: streaming-mux endpoint p95 from 180ms -> 680ms, p99 from 310ms -> 2.1s. Increase in page-faults and kv-evictions at the same time. Dashboard: https://grafana.company/d/streaming
AJ: grabbing logs from affected machines now. Quick tail of decode logs shows repeated `kv_pagefault: evict_after_decode` and many `cuda_sync` stalls. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T16:02:11Z decode: kv_pagefault evict_after_decode id=0x7fa
2026-03-15T16:02:11Z runtime: cuda_sync wait 2.04s kernel=flash_attn_forward
```
AJ: also seeing more frequent long-running kernels matching the new compilepath signature.
Maria: this smells like the new toolchain/compilepath interacting badly with our streaming decode path. Priority: mitigate customer impact ASAP. Options: rollback kernel/toolchain, route traffic to older pool, or temporary autoscale + slower model variant.
Kevin: rolling back the compilepath on all pools will take ~8-12m to fully drain if we trigger via auto-deploy. I can push a rollback to canary immediately.
Dave: runbook: see /runbooks/streaming-tail.md — section: "Kernel/compilepath regression". Hotpatch steps below (use carefully):
```
# rollback compilepath
./infra/deploy rollback --component=compilepath --target=prod --tag=toolchain-2026-03-14-0912
# or force route
./infra/route set --service=streaming --pool=legacy-kernel --percent=100
```
Maria: start the route fallback to legacy pool (route 50%) while we evaluate rollback. AJ, Kevin coordinate canary rollback. I'll notify SRE and Product about customer impact.
AJ: routing 50% now to legacy-pool: `./infra/route set --service=streaming --pool=legacy-kernel --percent=50` — observing initial p99 drop in eu-west.
Susan: eu-west p99 -> 1.1s after 50% shift. still high in us-west.
Kevin: canary rollback queued — starting in ~30s. watching compile pipeline.
sre-bot: Started job j-8421: compilepath rollback -> toolchain-2026-03-14-0912. ETA 9m.
Maria: good. AJ please collect a small perf profile comparing flash_attn kernel times before/after route change and after rollback. We need concrete delta for postmortem.
AJ: perf snippets attached (summary):
- legacy kernel flash_attn avg 12ms, p99 54ms
- toolchain-2026 flash_attn avg 28ms, p99 480ms
Kevin: rollback completed on canary. No regressions observed on canary now. Proceeding to rollout rollback to prod (gradual).
sre-bot: job j-8421: rollback rollout -> started, 0/128 hosts completed
Maria: start escalation if rollback fails. Also annotate tickets for customers: product please prepare comms for affected accounts (we estimate ~3% of requests saw >=2s latency; high-volume streaming customers: AcmeChat, ComposeAI)
Susan: running quick query: count of requests >2s over last 30m = ~12.4k (3.2% of streaming). Using retention traces to sample user ids for outreach.
Kevin: rollback is at 60% hosts; early signs show p99 trending down in both regions. Keep monitoring.
AJ: logging shows cuda_sync stalls largely disappear on hosts that rolled back. KV eviction rate drops ~70%.
Maria: great. Keep the rollback until we root-cause. Post-mortem owners: Kevin + AJ + Susan. Action items for now: 1) keep rollback, 2) revert aggressive compile flag, 3) run targeted tests on flash_attn with new toolchain to reproduce, 4) prepare fix or patch to kernel scheduling.
Dave: filing incident ticket INC-6165000, will link runbook and Grafana graphs. Also scheduling follow-up postmortem for tomorrow 09:30 PT.
sre-bot: job j-8421: rollback complete on 128/128 hosts. Duration 11m42s.
Maria: rollback complete :thumbsup:. SLOs returning to normal — p95 ~210ms, p99 ~320ms. We'll keep traffic on legacy kernel until we validate a safe compilepath.
Kevin: tentative root cause hypothesis: new compilepath triggers a suboptimal kernel variant for flash_attn under streaming batch sizes, causing excessive global memory syncs and page eviction patterns. Will dig into compiler flags and kernel selection heuristics.
AJ: collecting test harness reproducer. Will post link when available.
Maria: thanks team. Closing the page when we publish the incident ticket notes and postmortem. If anyone sees regressions re-open immediately. :white_check_mark:
